title: The rating that rewrote history
blurb: Feedback was attributed to the active model instead of the one that served it.
prompt: After a model rollout, last week's feedback silently moved to the new model because attribution fell back to the active version, and a double-clicked thumbs-up counted twice. The model-generated draft misattributes on lookup failure and dedupes with SISMEMBER-then-SADD. Review it, fix it, and prove feedback stays pinned to the request that earned it and counts once.
aiNote: The draft attributes unattributable feedback to whatever model is active at read time, so a rollout rewrites the past, and its non-atomic dedupe lets a double submit store two ratings under a key that ignores the tenant.
testIdea: Submit feedback for a request served by v1 after v2 becomes active and assert the record still reads v1; double-submit concurrently and assert one row; stub attribution to time out and assert the rating is stored as unattributed.
followUps: Should unattributed feedback count toward any model's score, and how do you decide?
How would you weight feedback from a power user versus a long-tail user?
What fingerprint of a comment is safe to keep for dedupe?
